Autoimmune parathyroid failure; cataract (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed complication. Hypercalciuria is not renal damage; paresthesias do not establish lasting nerve injury.
Drug-induced non-IgE hypersensitivity involves immune effector activation; transient skin or respiratory reactions do not establish lasting organ damage.

Benign reactive lymphoid nodules occupy lung; this is not lymphoma. Immunodeficiency and autoimmune findings are very rare (1-4%).
Progressive immune-mediated CNS demyelination; neurogenic bladder reflects neurological dysfunction, while optic neuritis is a separately diagnosed complication.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the prostate; lymphoma warrants blood-cell and immune axes. Prostate as a reproductive organ has no axis.
Malignant astrocytic tumour arising in the CNS.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect; encephalopathy and progressive neurological impairment, with seizures in 2/4; optic atrophy 2/4. Individual pulmonary findings occur in 1/4.

Inherited bile-acid transport disorder impairs ileal reabsorption, causing chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea and fat malabsorption; no evidence of hepatic injury.
Ovarian germ-cell tumour affects a reproductive organ; it is not inherently a disorder of ovarian hormone production.
Lysosomal storage disease with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss are common (>50%) over the juvenile disease course.
Frontonasal arterial-venous malformation; variable overlying skin changes, bleeding and visual symptoms do not establish common direct injury to additional organs.
Congenital enteroviral infection; available definition and ancestry do not establish specific organ damage in at least 30% of patients.
Inherited sleep-related frontal lobe epilepsy; no established extra-neurological organ involvement.
